The third part of the stars that the dragon’s tail swept away is represented by heretics, pagans, Jews, and false Christians, who are cast out of heaven—that is, from the fellowship of the saints—and dragged into the company of evil human beings.

They are signified by the stars pulled down from heaven. They once appeared to shine in the Church, but when Antichrist comes, deceived by flattery, torments, and false miracles, they will be darkened.

This casting down of the stars occurs every day, but it will happen then to a greater degree, in proportion to the savagery of the persecution. When it says “he swept away,” the past tense is used, according to the usage of sacred Scripture, in place of the future. Or he rightly says “he swept away a third of the stars,” because, looking back in a certain way, he speaks of the whole elapsed period. From the Lord’s coming, when the spiritual stars began to shine in heaven, these too began to fall.

**And the dragon stood before the woman who was about to give birth, so that when she had given birth he might devour her child.** With respect to blessed Mary, the devil stood before her, wishing to kill her Son through Herod, when he fled to Egypt and the infants were killed in his place. But what he could not do through that Herod, he did through his son Herod, who, as the Gospel says, was in Jerusalem in those days.

The devil wanted to devour him because, thinking that he was merely a human being, he supposed that he could hold him with the others in hell. But he could not, as is said later, because, rising from the dead, he ascended to God the Father.

So every day, indeed every hour, the devil stands before the holy Church, so that he may deceive those who, reborn through the baptismal font, become children of God. But he does not prevail, because they are snatched up to God, by whom they are protected, according to the saying: “Wherever the body is, there the eagles will also be gathered” (Matt. 24). And: “I desire that where I am, my servant may also be” (Matt. 24).

Neither Christ nor his members overcome the dragon only when they ascend to heaven. Rather, both the Lord himself and his elect overcome him in this life, because they keep the commandments of life. Hence we read in the Gospel that, when the devil tempted the Lord, he himself brought forward divine testimonies, and was thus confounded.

**And she gave birth to a male child.** Blessed Mary gave birth to a male child—that is, to the strong Lord Jesus Christ, who came for this purpose: to defeat the ruler of this world. Concerning him the Psalmist says: “The Lord is strong and mighty, the Lord mighty in battle.”

“Male” is sometimes used in a negative sense and sometimes in a positive one. In the negative sense, as in Jeremiah: “Cursed is the man who announced to my father, saying: ‘A male child has been born to you’” (Jer. 20). In that passage the prophet represents the human race, saying: “Cursed is the man”—that is, the devil—“who announced to my father,” the world, “a male child has been born to you”—that is, a people strong for evil.

Of this father the Psalmist says: “Hear, O daughter, and see,” and so forth, up to “the house of your father.” In this passage, however, “male” is used in a positive sense, because it signifies the Lord Jesus Christ—or certainly his members, whom the holy Church gives birth to every day.

The saints are rightly included under the name “male,” because they fight bravely against the adversities of this world, as did the holy apostles and martyrs, who even handed over their own bodies for Christ’s name. To them the Psalmist says: “Act manfully, and let your heart be strengthened” (Deut. 31).

**And the one who was to rule all the nations with an iron rod.** This can be understood both of Christ, who rules all nations with inflexible power, concerning whom it is said in the Psalm, “Ask of me, and I will give you the nations as your inheritance and the ends of the earth as your possession” (Ps. 2), and of all the elect, who received authority in their head to rule the nations with an iron rod.

They have authority to shatter them like a potter’s vessel, so that they may make vessels of mercy out of vessels of wrath. For what Christ does by his power, the saints also do by his gift, through their preaching.

The iron rod signifies the uprightness of justice. By it they love the good that God created and pursue the evil that human beings have wickedly committed. Thus they weigh their own deeds as though they were another’s, and judge the deeds of others as though they were their own.

**And her child was caught up to God and to his throne.** This rapture, as was said above, is not merely bodily but also spiritual. For there is, as it were, a rapture of the saints from this world to God when, by keeping the commandments of life, they adorn outwardly in their works the faith they possess inwardly. Hence the Psalmist says: “He has arranged ascents in his heart.”

**And the woman fled into the wilderness, where she has a place prepared by God, so that there they might feed her for 1,260 days.** The wilderness to which the woman fled must be understood as the hidden place of the mind. When she first casts away the tumult of earthly desires and the excessive cares of this world, she makes herself a desert of repose. There she finds a place prepared by God—that is, God almighty himself, who rests in her heart.

This is the place of which the Psalmist says: “Be for me a protecting God and a place of refuge, so that you may save me” (Ps. 30). In the wilderness of the heart the saints find a place in which they may be saved, because, while they do not suffer the insolence of thoughts and seek only eternal things, they have their Creator dwelling in the hidden place of their hearts.

In that wilderness they feed her—without doubt, the holy preachers are understood here, who feed the Church by their preaching and teaching for 1,260 days. Although this number specifically pertains to the times of Antichrist, during which the Church will necessarily be fed by teachers, especially Elijah and Enoch, it can also refer to the whole present age, from the Lord’s ascension to the end of the world.

During this period, while the Church dwells in the wilderness of her Creator and rests from the cares of temporal affairs, teachers feed her by example and teaching through their Epistles, the Gospel, and expositions of the books, as with the nourishment of the divine word.

For just as Antichrist will reign for 1,260 days, so Christ preached for 1,260 days—that is, three years and six months. Therefore, by this number we can understand the whole present period, from the time when divine preaching began until the time when it will be completed by the final preachers.

Long ago this woman was signified by the people who came out of Egypt. Fleeing Pharaoh—the dragon who lay among his rivers—they were led into the desert, where they ate manna and were delivered from the bites of fiery serpents by looking upon the bronze serpent suspended on a tree.

That desert signified the present life and the hidden wildernesses of the mind. In this life we are nourished by the true manna, that is, by the body of Christ, who says: “I am the living bread that came down from heaven,” and so forth, “for the life of the world.”

There are also fiery serpents—that is, demons—who try to pour the poison of their wickedness into us. But they do not prevail, because we are delivered by him who, suspended on the cross, freed us from the devil. He also bore the likeness of our mortality, yet did not possess the stain of sin; therefore he is able to cleanse us from every sin.

And a great battle took place in heaven. The battle did not take place only when, at the beginning of time, the devil was cast down from heaven through pride, but also when, after the Lord’s Passion, he was cast out from the hearts of the faithful and began to rage more fiercely against everyone; and this battle continues until the end of the world, when, after he has been released, it will be brought to completion. For heaven is the holy Church, in which this battle takes place, especially—as we have said—since he was expelled through faith from the hearts of believers, when the apostles preached, in accordance with the words: “Our struggle is not against flesh and blood,” and so forth. Thus it is said: “A great battle took place in heaven,” so that it may be believed without any doubt that the whole period of the present life—from the beginning of the Christian faith to the end—is encompassed: that it took place in the past, exists in the present, and will be completed in the last days.

Michael and his angels fought with the dragon. The angels are said to belong to Michael or to the dragon, and to have been subjected and sent to obey them, not created by them, as certain heretical windbags have said; or else because they are believed to serve under one king in one city. Thus we too are accustomed to say, when we see those who belong to the same association, “Look, mine,” or “ours.” Hence the Lord says in the Gospel concerning the little ones: “Their angels always see the face of my Father who is in heaven” (Matt. XVIII). Hence Joshua asks the commander of the Lord’s army, saying: “Are you for us, or for our adversaries?” All the good angels are called Michael’s angels because they belong to his fellowship. Within this number of good angels righteous human beings who fight against the devil are also included.

The angels of the dragon, on the other hand, are all those who agreed with him when, in his pride, he said: “I will ascend above the heights of heaven,” and so forth. The form of wicked human beings is likewise included there. Thus Michael and his angels fight in heaven—that is, in the Church—and the dragon fights with his demons, because just as the demons are always ready to attack, so the holy angels are ready to resist. Nevertheless, neither do we fight against the ancient enemy without the angels, nor do the angels fight without our conflict. Let us therefore raise our weapons without fear, because we have as fellow citizens the strongest defenders of our homeland and unconquered helpers, in accordance with what the Apostle says: “Are they not all ministering spirits sent out for service, for the sake of those who are to inherit salvation?” From the same source comes their strength as ours; from the same source their invincibility as ours—that is, from divine power, without which neither they nor we can accomplish anything.

For now Michael, who is placed over the Church, fights with his angels on behalf of the Church. He will also fight more intensely at the time of Antichrist, in accordance with the words: “At that time Michael, your prince, will arise,” and so forth.  
[Col. 1085C–D; 1086A–B]

And they did not prevail, nor was their place found any longer in heaven. Why does he say “they did not prevail,” when even after baptism and his renunciation the devil deceives many? Although they may appear to prevail for a time, nevertheless they do not prevail against those who are predestined for life, because, when sin has been removed through repentance, the devil finds no place in them. That person becomes his dwelling in whose mind sin reigns. Take away, therefore, the reign of sin, and no place for the devil will be found.

There are also some against whom they do not prevail even temporarily, because they cannot trip them into any mortal crime by which they ought to possess their hearts. To such people Paul says: “Do not give place to the devil.” This may also be referred specifically to the day of judgment, when their battle, from the Lord’s coming in judgment, will be brought to an end. Once this has occurred, the statement will be fulfilled: “They did not prevail”—that is, at the end of the battle they will succumb. “Nor was their place found any longer in heaven,” because then, having been utterly excluded from the elect, they will no longer have an opportunity to deceive them.

And that great dragon was cast down, the ancient serpent, who is called the Devil and Satan. As has already been said, that ancient enemy is called a dragon because of the enormity of his crime, great because of his hidden snares, and the ancient serpent because, through the first serpent, he deceived the first human being by fraud and thus destroyed him with the poison of wickedness. He is also called the Devil—that is, “flowing downward,” or “the accuser”—because every day he flows away from the hearts of the faithful. He is called Satan—that is, “the adversary”—because he persecutes the good, whose works are opposed to his.

Who deceives the whole world. This means, namely, those who perish—that is, a part of the world. For we must understand a part from the whole: although he often deceives many of the elect in heart, he does not deceive them perpetually or unto eternal death.

And he was cast down to the earth. He was cast down from heaven to earth—that is, from the minds of the elect into the hearts of the reprobate—not because he was not already in them as well, but because, having been expelled from the former, he began to dominate the latter more fully. The earth receives his downfall because he invades the minds of those who seek earthly things and think earthly thoughts. Concerning this earth, the same serpent is figuratively told in the first curse: “You shall eat earth all the days of your life.” For when the Prophet says, “His food is the elect,” this must be understood of those who appeared elect in human estimation but were already earth in the sight of God.  
[Col. 1086C–D; 1087A]

And I heard a loud voice from heaven saying: “Now salvation and power and the kingdom of our God, and the authority of his Christ, have come.” This voice concerns the whole present age. It began with the advent of the Redeemer, but it does not cease to cry out until it reaches completion. Thus this voice in heaven is the great desire of the elect in the Church: “Now salvation has come.” Throughout the whole period of the present life—from the advent of the Mediator to the end of that same preaching—salvation has come, because we have been saved by the grace or goodness of God. Hence the Psalmist says: “Salvation belongs to the Lord,” and so forth. “Power has come,” because through him we have been strengthened. The kingdom and authority of our God have also come, just as he himself says after rising from the dead: “All authority in heaven and on earth has been given to me” (Matt. XXVIII).

Because the accuser of our brothers has been cast down, who accused them before the presence of our God day and night. The devil’s accusation is nothing other than driving someone headlong into evil. He accuses when he makes people worthy of accusation—not by speaking outwardly, but by hating inwardly. But the person appears free from this accusation who strives to accuse in himself what he knows can be accused by his adversary.

Therefore the angels, rejoicing at our restoration, rejoice at the devil’s fall. Hence, at the Lord’s birth, they said: “Glory to God in the highest.” For why should it be surprising that they call human beings brothers, when they see the Lord himself doing this? Rising from the dead, he says to Mary: “Go, tell my brothers.” For the angels no longer disdain to have human beings as brothers, since they have the Lord as a human brother.

By “day and night” either continuous time is understood, or prosperity and adversity. The devil accuses by day and night when he exalts some in prosperity and breaks others through adversity, and he does this before the presence of God, who is everywhere, in accordance with the words: “I fill heaven and earth.”

And they conquered him. That is, the saints who are in the Church and in heaven wage war against the dragon—that is, in the fellowship of the elect.

Because of the blood of the Lamb. That is, they imitate his Passion by putting themselves to death together with their vices and desires.

And because of the word of their testimony. Because they preserve the uprightness of faith.

And they did not love their lives unto death. Because they chose to die in this life so that afterward they might reign with Christ rather than live here temporarily and afterward perish eternally. They surrendered themselves unto death so that they might not wickedly love their lives. Hence Paul said: “For I am ready not only to be bound, but also to die for Christ, and I do not regard my life as more precious than myself” (Acts XX). And the Lord says: “Whoever loves his life will lose it.” For they imitate their Lord, whom they know did not spare his life for their redemption.  
[Col. 1087A–C; 1088A–B]

Therefore rejoice, heavens—that is, all the churches. They use the plural number because they indicate the multitude of the churches.

And you who dwell in them. That is, all the saints who remain in the assembly of the saints. Or certainly, by the inhabitants of heaven we may understand the angels, with whom it is fitting to rejoice together in the Lord, since human beings return to their fellowship and the angels see their own number restored when these are received. There is nothing else that needs to be explained here, except that, with this joy remaining, the book should reach its proper conclusion.

# BOOK FOUR

[Col. 1087]

## CHAPTER XII FOLLOWS

[Col. 1087C]

Woe to the earth and the sea, because the devil has come down to you with great wrath. Earth and sea signify one and the same thing, as Daniel plainly demonstrates. When he had said that he saw four winds fighting upon the great sea, he added: “And four beasts came up from the earth.” He signifies by earth the same thing as by sea: this world, in which the wretched are tossed about, who always seek earthly things.

Thus here too earth and sea signify the hearts of the reprobate, upon whom there is woe—that is, eternal damnation or destruction. To them the crafty enemy, expelled from the elect, has descended—not because he was not previously in them, but because, expelled from those who were not his, he began to dominate his own more fully. They are rightly called earth and sea because, while they always seek earthly things, they are found swollen with the waves of pride and exceedingly bitter through the allurements of vices.

Woe therefore—that is, eternal damnation—threatens such people, because the devil, cast down from the faithful, rages against them with great wrath. And the more fiercely he does this, the nearer he senses his punishment to be. Hence it is added: “Knowing that he has only a short time.” The short time means the present life, concerning which the Apostle says: “Little children, it is the last hour” (1 John II). Even if we reckon all time from the beginning of the world to its end, it is exceedingly brief when compared with eternity.

Because the devil knows that he is soon to be condemned, this time seems narrow to him for exercising his malice, however long he may extend it through drawn-out intervals of delay. He considers that it is near when he will lose the license of his most wicked freedom; and the more he is confined by the brevity of time, the more widely he expands through the multiplicity of his crimes.

We must believe that this downfall of his took place both at the advent of our Redeemer and continues to take place even now. The devil has wrath not only against those who are represented by earth and sea, but also against those who dwell in heaven, by whom he is defeated and excluded. For through the latter as well he rages more craftily against the former.  
[Col. 1087D; 1088C–D; 1089A]

And when the dragon saw that he had been cast down from heaven—that is, from the bodies of the elect—into the earth, that is, into the hearts of the reprobate, he pursued the woman who had given birth to the male child.

The holy Church is signified by heaven, and likewise by the woman. She is called a woman not because of softness of spirit, but because she never ceases daily to give birth to spiritual children for God. She is the bride betrothed by the ring of faith in baptism, concerning whom Paul says: “For I betrothed you to one husband, to present you as a pure virgin to Christ” (2 Cor. XI). And elsewhere: “Christ betrothed to himself a Church without spot or wrinkle” (Eph. V). In the following words of this book it is also said: “Come, I will show you the bride of the Lamb” (Rev. XXI).

She is also the wife established in perfection of work and conduct, because through her preaching and teaching she generates many children for God. Hence the Lord himself says: “Whoever does the will of my Father, that person is my brother, sister, and mother” (Mark III). By believing, therefore, she becomes the bride; by adhering to works, the wife; by preaching with her voice, the mother of Christ. For she gives birth to Christ as often as, through the duty of preaching, she forms his members—which are ourselves—for faith and action.

When the dragon saw, therefore, that he had been cast down from heaven, especially after the coming of the Son of God, concerning whom the Lord says: “I saw Satan falling from heaven like lightning,” he pursued the woman who had given birth to the male child—that is, the strong people, such as the holy martyrs, who were able to die rather than be separated from the faith of God.

He pursued this woman in her very youth, when he killed Abel; but after the coming of the Son of God he began to persecute her more fiercely and, as a device of persecution, cunningly devoted himself to it: crucifying some through his members, as Peter; crushing others with stones, as Stephen; consuming others with fire, as Laurence; handing still others over to serpents; tearing them with claws; casting them into the sea; and compelling them to pass through various instruments of torment of the same kind.

He does these things while bound, but he will rise up against her more violently when he enters the condemned man and fights with torments and false signs of miracles, so that, if possible, even the elect may be led into error (Matt. XXIV). Their steadfastness will then be all the stronger in proportion to the monstrous savagery of their persecutors.  
[Col. 1089B–D]

And two great wings like those of an eagle were given to the woman, so that she might fly into the wilderness, to her place. The two wings given to the woman signify the two Testaments and the two commandments of charity, on which the whole Law and the Prophets depend, or also the active and contemplative life. Having received these, she became an eagle, seeking heavenly things through contemplation of the mind, in accordance with the Apostle’s words: “Our citizenship is in heaven” (Phil. III).

Thus it is said: “Two wings like those of a great eagle were given to the woman,” as though it were said: This gift was granted to the woman, that she might become a great eagle.

The wilderness signifies the hearts of the saints, removed from earthly desires. First they cast out from themselves the disordered movements of desire, and thus make themselves a wilderness of quiet, so that they may have a place to which they can flee. Because they do not love the evils of this world but desire only their eternal homeland, they enjoy great tranquillity of mind.

In this solitude there is a place to which the person who flees may go to God, who is found in the secrecy of the mind by those who seek him. To him the Psalmist says: “Be for me a protecting God and a place of refuge, so that you may save me” (Ps. LXX).

Using the two wings, therefore, the woman escapes the dragon’s persecution, because the holy Church, supported by knowledge of the two Testaments or by the two commandments of charity, and lifted toward heavenly things, knows how to avoid the enemy’s hidden snares and to despise his open persecutions. She removes herself from all the turmoil of earthly affairs and devotes herself to the Lord in the secrecy of the mind.

There she is nourished for a time and times and half a time, away from the face of the serpent. That is, throughout the whole period of this life, from the Lord’s preaching to the end of the world, by that bread which came down from heaven. For he himself is the way for those fleeing the savagery of persecutors; he himself is the place for those reaching the wilderness; he himself is food for those hungering in that same wilderness.

Enough has been said above concerning this period. Since Christ’s preaching lasted three and a half years, and will be brought to an end after three and a half years, this interval rightly signifies the whole period of the present life, during which the Church remains under the same teaching.

In the figure of this woman, the people of Israel were once led by a pillar of cloud during the day and a pillar of fire during the night. In the cloud, the gentleness of love is expressed; in the fire, the terror of fear. Through these two pillars the two Testaments are signified.

By the cloud during the day, the New Testament is signified, in which not the vengeance of sinners but the gentleness of mercy was displayed. Hence the saying: “No one has condemned you, woman” (John VIII). By the fire during the night, the Old Testament is understood, which threatens punishment to sinners. Hence the saying: “If anyone does this or that, let him die the death.”

The people fleeing from Pharaoh, who is the great dragon lying in the midst of his rivers, just as the woman flees from the dragon, reached the wilderness, where they found God as their protector, were fed with heavenly manna, and were saved through the suspended bronze serpent—that is, the Lord Jesus Christ, who was free from the poison of sin. For although he appeared in the likeness of sinful flesh, he did not commit sin, nor was deceit found in his mouth (1 Pet. II).

The name wilderness may also designate that region which the apostate angel deserted, and the human being in whom the Church found a secure place of refuge. On earth she is pressed on every side by persecutions, yet there she finds unfailing food; while afflicted here, she hungers for righteousness.

In the woman’s wings, the very elevation of contemplation is understood. This is ordinarily a particular gift of the saints: the more they are pressed by afflictions on earth, the more greatly they are lifted by the feather of contemplation toward the heights. Hence Paul says: “When I am weak, then I am strong” (2 Cor. XII).

And the serpent cast from his mouth after the woman water like a river. In Sacred Scripture, the force of waters often signifies persecution. Hence the Psalmist says: “When their anger was enraged against us, perhaps the water would have swallowed us” (Ps. CXXIII).

By the mouth of the ancient serpent, his persuasion is understood, by which the reprobate are incited to rage against the Church. Therefore, after the woman flying into the wilderness, the serpent sent out a river from his mouth, because especially after the coming of the Son of God, and after the Church sought heavenly things, the devil stirred up a multitude of unbelievers for the slaughter of the saints—such as Nero, Domitian, and others—so that he might cause her to be carried away by the river, that is, into his own body, namely, into the fellowship of the reprobate. But he was unable to do so, because although the martyrs die in body, after the death of the flesh they will truly say: “Our soul has passed through the torrent” (ibid.). For when the persecutors were unable to draw them into their own body, they tried utterly to destroy them.  
[Col. 1090A–D; 1091A–B]

And the earth helped the woman. In sacred speech, earth signifies human nature. Hence it was said to the first human being: “You are earth, and into earth you shall go.” Earth therefore signifies here the flesh of our Redeemer, who, although he was in the form of God, took the form of a servant. Concerning this earth the Psalmist says: “You have blessed your land, O Lord” (Ps. LXXXIV).

This earth helped the woman because he himself first endured and conquered all the waves of human persecution. And the earth opened its mouth and swallowed the river that the dragon sent from his mouth. For at the time of his Passion, by the abundance of his life he swallowed the prince of death; and, rising from the dead, by the power of his divinity he swallowed the overflowing waves, because he died for this purpose: that he might be Lord of both the living and the dead. Hence the Apostle says: “God gave him the name that is above every name, so that at the name of Jesus every knee should bow” (Phil. II).

From the point at which he overcame the waves of persecution, he also helped the Church so that she could not be conquered, as though he were saying to his faithful: “Do not fear death; do not fear entering the waves of human persecutions. Rather, have confidence, because I have conquered the world; I have also defeated the prince of the world; by rising again I have trampled the waves of mortal life, because I first drank his persecutions and, by drinking, overcame them, and I gave you hope of rising again.

“Therefore, just as I humbled myself and came to victory through humility, so follow humility, that afterward you may be able to reign with me, since the devil will have no greater power over the body than he had over the head.”

And the dragon became angry with the woman. That is, against the holy Church, which, as I have said, is called a woman because she gives birth to spiritual children.

And he went off to wage war with the rest of her offspring. The dragon did wage war with those who were good before the Lord’s advent, such as Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob, and many others. But after the coming of the Son of God he began to rage more fiercely against the rest who were from her offspring—that is, against the apostles and martyrs, whom he crucified, burned, handed over to fire, and tortured with various torments through his members.

The offspring of the woman is understood as the word of preaching, through which human beings are reborn and become children of God. The more the devil was defeated by those strengthened by divine grace before them, the more fiercely he raged against the members of the Church. Hence it is said that, having been expelled from a person, he returns with seven other spirits more wicked than himself.

Who keep the commandments of God. In the Law they are commanded: “You shall not kill; you shall not steal,” and other things of this kind.

And hold the testimony of Jesus. That is, they retain his faith in their hearts and adorn it through their works. The devil has his greatest conflict with such people, in accordance with the Apostle’s words: “All who wish to live devoutly in Christ suffer persecution” (2 Tim. III).

The reprobate also suffer evils, but the devil does not direct warfare against them, since this cannot happen except between two opposing sides. Yet when it is first said that they keep the Lord’s commandments and then added, “and the faith of Jesus,” the words seem to sound as though good works could exist before faith, whereas one must first believe and then support that same faith with works.

It must be understood, however, that the commandments are placed first because charity, which consists in the commandments, is greater than all the virtues, although faith is the way to God. Hence the Apostle says: “Now faith, hope, and charity remain, these three; but the greatest of these is charity” (1 Cor. XIII). Why is it greater? Because the others will pass away, while charity will remain in the elect.  
[Col. 1091C–D; 1092A–B]

And he stood upon the sand of the sea. It should be noted that the same dragon is said to have stood not upon a rock but upon the sand. It is clear to everyone that a serpent cannot leave a trace upon rock. But wherever it touches the sand, it leaves marks of its body.

The dragon does not stand upon rock because the devil finds no place in the hearts of the saints, which no pleasures soften. By contrast, he fixes his step upon sand because he inhabits minds softened by the moisture of carnal desire. Hence the Lord says to Job: “He sleeps under the shade in the secret place of the reed, in moist places” (Job XL)—that is, he rests in slippery and pleasure-loving hearts. Therefore the one whom the Lord forbids to sleep in moist places, John affirms to stand upon the sand.

# CHAPTER XIII

And I saw from the sea. That is, from the multitude of the reprobate, or from the deep faithlessness of the Jews.

A beast ascending. That is, Antichrist. Whenever “beast” is used in the singular in sacred speech, the prince of the wicked spirits is designated through it. Hence the saying: “The beast of the field will tear them.” And Isaiah says: “No evil beast will pass through it.” But where the term is used in a particular or plural sense, either all the monstrous manifestations of demons or the bestial movements of human beings are expressed. Hence the saying: “All the beasts of the field will play there.” And the Apostle says: “If, speaking in human terms, I fought with beasts at Ephesus.” And: “Cretans are always liars, evil beasts.”

Here, therefore, as I have said, the beast that rises from the sea signifies the devil, who rises from the hearts of the reprobate in order to rage more fiercely, having been released through the lost man who will be born from the Jewish people, in accordance with the words: “Let Dan be a serpent on the way,” and so forth, “so that his rider may fall backward” (Gen. XLIX). In him also his entire body is represented.

Having seven heads and ten horns, and upon his horns ten diadems. By the seven heads all the kings subject to him are understood; by the ten horns, all the kingdoms. He will have many powers of this age subject to him, and he will bestow honor upon them; and, with the Lord permitting it, he will possess the kingdoms of the world. Hence there are ten diadems upon his horns. For “ten diadems” signifies the same as “ten horns”: all earthly kingdoms subject to him. We find that the seven heads or horns signify universality, not number.

And upon his heads a name written: blasphemy. For the powers of this world chiefly blaspheme God in word and deed. He himself will blaspheme God, his tabernacle, and his name, as we shall find later. Those who are his members will do this as well, because they desire to please him.

Concerning this blasphemy the Apostle says that he “will oppose and exalt himself above everything that is called God or worshiped, so that he takes his seat in the temple of God, presenting himself as God.” His members will also worship him, because they will give him divine honor. And because the beast signifies not only the head but also his entire body, it is added:

And the beast that I saw was like a leopard, and its feet were like the feet of a bear, and its mouth was like the mouth of a lion. The leopard is an exceedingly savage and impatient beast, and its coat is marked with varied colors. The bear is also extremely rapacious: first it tramples and crushes with its feet, and then devours everything. The lion, moreover, strikes all beasts with terror by its roar; and although it is the strongest of beasts and fears no encounter, it nevertheless seizes its prey by lying in wait.

Such are the heretics, pagans, and others who belong to the body of Antichrist. In the leopard’s variety, the diversity of the nations that will believe him is shown. Or it may signify the abundance of riches with which he will adorn his subjects. Or certainly it may signify the fabricated actions of all hypocrites and all the reprobate, who always want the good things they do to be seen, so that they may receive praise from human beings.

Hence the Lord says to the faithful: “When you pray, do not speak at length, as the hypocrites do. And when you give alms, do not sound a trumpet before you, as the hypocrites do; but let your left hand not know what your right hand is doing” (Matt. VI). The righteous are also commanded to display their works, but so that they themselves may not be glorified through them; rather, the heavenly Father may be glorified.

In the bear, secular power is expressed. Hence we read appropriately in the Book of Kings that, when Elisha was returning to Bethel, boys mocking him began to say: “Go up, baldhead; go up, baldhead” (2 Kings II). Therefore he cursed them in the name of the Lord, and two bears came out of the forest and devoured forty-two of the boys.

Elisha signifies the Lord Jesus in this passage. When he was returning to the Father through the Passion of death, the mocking boys—that is, the Jews, who thought in a childish manner—shouted insults at him, saying: “Ha! You who destroy the temple of God and rebuild it in three days. If he is the Son of God, let him now come down from the cross, and we will believe him” (Matt. XXVII).

But when the Lord’s blood demanded vengeance, two bears—Titus and Vespasian, leaders of the nations—came forth with a multitude of armies after the forty-second year of the Lord’s Passion and destroyed the Jewish people. Just as earthly power is expressed there by the bear, so also here. Such are those in the body of Antichrist who, with the feet of secular power, trample upon the poor, the weak, orphans, and the other servants of God.

The lion also, as we have said, although it is the strongest of beasts and fears no encounter, nevertheless lays snares when it seizes its prey. All beasts are said to fear its roar, and therefore Antichrist is rightly understood through the lion, because he deceives some by terrors and others by fraud. Hence the Psalmist says: “Under his tongue are trouble and pain” (Ps. X). “He sits in ambush with the rich in secret places.” Concerning him the same Psalmist says again: “Like a lion in his lair.”

The ancient adversary, placed in battle against the elect, is rightly called a lion because he is permitted to rage in both ways: by fraud and by force. By force, through secular power; by fraud, through signs of miracles. To draw in those who are openly wicked, he displays secular power; but in order also to deceive the righteous, he simulates holiness through signs. To the former he persuades arrogance through displays of greatness; the latter he deceives by an exhibition of holiness.

And the dragon gave him his power and great authority. Just as the fullness of divinity dwells in Christ, so the fullness of wickedness dwells in him. And just as Christ accomplishes all his works through the power of the Word, so the lost man will perform his works through the power of the devil who will dwell in him.

Thus the dragon—that is, the devil—gave him his power and strength, so that he might perform unheard-of miracles and signs. He gave him great authority, by which he will be lifted above nations and kingdoms. He will rage against the good, and there will be no difficulty in carrying out evil, because the one who invented every evil in himself will dwell in him.  
[Col. 1092C–D; 1093A–D; 1094A–C]

And I saw one of his heads as though slain unto death. Above we said that the seven heads designate all the kings subject to him. By the one head, however, which John says he saw individually as though slain, we must understand the prince of evils himself.

Hence it is rightly said that he saw him “as though slain unto death,” because he will pretend that he has been killed and has risen again after death. Hence it follows: “And the wound of his death was healed.” Such will be the audacity of that condemned man that, in order to deceive the minds of the simple, by imitating Christ, the true head, he will claim that he was killed and rose again after death.

Therefore, lest it be thought that this is truth rather than illusion, it is not stated affirmatively: “One of his heads was slain unto death, and the wound of his death was healed.” Rather, the word “as though” is prefixed—that is, the adverb of likeness—so that, through this, as has been said, it may plainly be shown that the event is not real but a deceptive appearance. Nevertheless, that particle is not always used in Scripture as an adverb of likeness; sometimes it is also used to affirm truth. Hence the saying: “We saw his glory, glory as of the only-begotten from the Father.”

And the whole earth marveled after the beast. There is no doubt that by the earth earthly-minded people are understood: they marvel after the beast, believing that it has risen from the dead and performs those miracles by the power of divinity.  
[Col. 1094D–1095A]

And they worshiped the dragon—that is, the devil—who gave authority to the beast to perform miracles with power. And they worshiped the beast—that is, Antichrist himself—saying: “Who is like the beast?”—so that he may show himself to have risen from the dead. “And who will be able to fight against it?”—so that anyone might be able to resist its will; that is, no one.

Here it is now plainly demonstrated what it means that the whole earth marvels after the beast: it means the reprobate and those who think earthly thoughts. They worshiped the dragon because they believed that the beast—namely, Antichrist—was Christ, supported not only by riches and powers but also by the signs and miraculous powers of the elect.

Perhaps he would be despised if he were supported only by secular power and not by miraculous powers as well. Again, perhaps he would be disregarded if he used only simulated miraculous powers and not secular power too. But when he appears supported by both signs and power, who would not tremble—not only among the reprobate but even among the elect? Hence those who worship him say: “Who is like the beast?”

And those who worship this beast speak truly in saying this, because in neither secular power nor the fraud of miracles has anything like him appeared in former times.  
[Col. 1095A–B]

And a mouth speaking great things and blasphemies was given to him. By the divine and just judgment of God, Antichrist is permitted to speak great things in order to deceive the minds of the reprobate—great things, certainly, not because they are good, but because they are unheard-of and terrifying. He will speak blasphemies because he will say that he is God and will make himself be worshiped as God.

It was also given to him by God that he should do this—that is, it was permitted to him. This is like the statement: “The heart of Pharaoh was hardened.”

And authority was given to him to act for forty-two months. Three and a half years contain forty-two months, and therefore the final period and the persecution of Antichrist are specifically signified by these months. In general, however, the whole period of this age—from the Lord’s preaching to the end of the world—is signified, just as above by the 1,260 days.

Because, therefore, the whole period during which the devil fights against the Church—or even the period during which, having been openly released, he will fight more fiercely—is understood through the forty-two months, we must consider, in the nature of this number itself, why he does not conquer them.

This number is composed of ten, four, and two. The four therefore refer to the four books of the Gospel, or to the four principal virtues. The ten refers to the Decalogue of the Law, and the two to the two commandments of love.

For this reason they remain unconquerable, whether throughout the whole period of the present life or under Antichrist: strengthened by the four books of the Gospel and fortified by the four principal virtues, they fulfill the Decalogue of the Law in action and keep the two commandments of love, loving the Lord their God with all their heart and their neighbor as themselves.

That the whole period of this life is also designated by the number forty-two is clear from the fact that the children of Israel entered the promised land after their forty-second encampment. It must be carefully noted by everyone that the journey of the people of Israel signifies the present life, in which we are pilgrims and journey toward our heavenly homeland.  
[Col. 1095C–D; 1096A]

And it opened its mouth in blasphemies against God, to blaspheme his name. The one who has now opened the mouths of the reprobate to blaspheme God or God’s servants will then open his mouth bodily, when he begins to dwell in that condemned man. For this is like what is said in the Gospel concerning our Redeemer—although there it is expressed oppositely: “Opening his mouth, he taught them” [Col. 1096B]—as though it said: “The one who had previously opened the mouths of the prophets, appearing in the presence of the flesh, opened his own mouth.” But the Lamb will open his mouth for teaching, whereas the beast will open its mouth for blasphemies.

Or certainly, because now, through his members, he does not dare to blaspheme openly, out of fear of the faithful people, his mouth is said to be obstructed, as the Psalmist says: “The mouth of those who speak iniquity has been stopped” (Ps. 62). He is said to open his mouth in the future, when, through that condemned man—raised up by worldly power against God and the Church—he will have dared publicly to blaspheme his name. This is the name of which Paul says: “Therefore God exalted him,” and so forth, up to “Our Lord Jesus Christ is in the glory of God the Father.” He will blaspheme this name, because he will say that the one is not Christ but rather Antichrist, while he himself will confess that he is Christ. No longer merely “like God,” but, as the Apostle says, “he will exalt and raise himself above everything that is called God or is worshiped”; therefore in him blasphemy is found in a form worse than in all others.

And his tabernacle—“he will blaspheme” is understood—that is, the very flesh of our Redeemer, in which the whole fullness of divinity dwells. He will say that things were not as they appear, but that it was a sign, and that he was able to accomplish such things through the power of demons. He will confess himself truly to be the Son of God and the son of man, so that he may sit in the temple of God as though he were God. And because he says that divinity dwells in him, he will therefore also cause himself to be worshiped.

And he will blaspheme those who dwell in heaven—that is, in the Church—whether those who live now or those who have already gone before [Col. 1096D]. He will say that all these were ministers of Antichrist, and that they were false prophets and apostles deceived by him, asserting that before him there had been no Christian, but that all had been Antichrists.

And it was given to him—that is, it was permitted to him by God’s just judgment—to wage war against the saints and to conquer them. He will wage war against the saints because he will fight against them with gifts, tortures, and torments; and those whom he cannot bend to his faith he will conquer—that is, he will kill them—though he will not deceive their souls.

But perhaps someone asks why almighty God permits his saints to be afflicted in this way. The brief answer is that they are sons, beloved by God, who are to be granted a paternal inheritance. Hence it is written: “God scourges every son whom he receives” (Heb. 12). For if the Lord himself, who is entirely without sin, endured persecution in order to attain glory, how much more are the saints afflicted by just judgment so that they may obtain the inheritance of the heavenly homeland? Although they are saints, they are nevertheless not without sin. The reprobate, by contrast, rage against them and continually do evil, yet are not corrected in the least. But at the judgment these people, toward whom he now appears to be angry, will find him reconciled, whereas the reprobate will experience him as angry. The anger that now mercifully begins with the saints comes to rest upon the reprobate without mercy. Hence Peter says (1 Pet. 4): “It is time for judgment to begin from the house of God.”

We may understand these saints as those who now appear to possess a feigned holiness in the sight of human beings. He will conquer them because, overcome by gifts or torments, they will withdraw from the faith that they now hold hypocritically.

And authority was given to him over every tribe, language, and nation. By “tribe” and “people” we understand the Jews, because that people was divided into tribes; by “language” and “nation,” all peoples. There will be saints not only among the Jews but also among all nations, against whom he will receive authority, so that he may kill them and prevail over them temporarily. Likewise, among both Jews and nations there will be those who are conquered and succumb. Hence what follows:

And they will worship him—that is, Antichrist—and, in him, the devil. All who dwell on the earth—that is, those who serve earthly desires—will worship him. Their names are not written in the book of life of the Lamb, but rather on the earth, according to what Jeremiah says (ch. 13): “Those who depart from you shall be written in the earth.”

But who the Lamb is, John makes clear when he says: “Behold the Lamb of God; behold, he who takes away the sins of the world” (John 1). What, then, is the Lamb’s book of life, in which the names of the righteous are reckoned and inscribed, if not a certain divine power that, before the foundation of the world, predestined the saints who were to come to eternal life? This book of predestination holds the elect inscribed in fixed eternity, and in no way admits the reprobate to be written in it.

Who was slain from the foundation of the world. This Lamb was slain from the foundation of the world—not in himself, but in his members, as in Abel and many others. For just as he is nourished in his members, so he is slain in his members. Hence the words: “Saul, Saul, why are you persecuting me?” (Acts 9).

Or certainly, he was slain in predestination, because before all the ages God the Father, with the Son and the Holy Spirit, decreed that he would come at the end of time and be slain, so that by his death he might redeem our death. Or he was slain in the lamb that Abel offered; or, to speak more truly, Abel himself, innocent and killed by his brother, prefigured him.

If anyone has ears—“of the heart” is understood—let him hear; that is, let him understand spiritually what is being said. Whenever this expression occurs, whether in the Gospel or in this Apocalypse, the things that precede or follow it are to be understood spiritually.

Whoever leads into captivity will go into captivity. These words apply both to the whole body of Antichrist and to Antichrist himself, the prince of evils [Col. 1098A]. He will take human beings captive in two ways: first, separating them in mind from the faith of Christ; then, separating them from the fellowship of the faithful and the eternal realities. Those who obey him will be condemned to the perpetual exile of captivity. He too will first be taken captive in soul, when he is handed over to the devil for possession; then he will be condemned in hell to everlasting captivity.

Whoever kills with the sword must be killed with the sword. This too is to be understood in two ways. First, he will kill human beings in soul with the sword of evil persuasion; then, those whom he cannot overcome in this way, he will kill with a material sword. With that same sword he will also slaughter Elijah and Enoch.

The Psalmist desired to be delivered from this spiritual sword when he said to God: “Deliver me from the evil sword” (Ps. 143). He too will be killed by the sword of the divine sentence, according to the words: “The Lord Jesus Christ will kill him with the breath of his mouth.” It is as though he were saying to the martyrs: “Do not be afraid; do not tremble; do not become faint-hearted. Rather, be strong against the strong, because what you are suffering will soon pass, and those from whom you suffer will swiftly receive vengeance”—that is, the devil and his condemned man, or the whole multitude of the reprobate, who are in fact one.

Here is the patience—that is why the saints preserve the virtue of patience even amid adversity: they know that in a little while they will triumph, and that, once he who had prevailed over them for a time has been condemned, they themselves will rejoice forever. And the faith of the saints—“here is,” is understood—because their reward and the condemnation of the impious will certainly and justly be fulfilled [Col. 1098C].

And I saw another beast ascending from the earth. The first beast is Antichrist himself, the head of the wicked; the second is understood as his body, especially those who will preach him. They are said to ascend from the earth because, from the earthly advantages and riches they will possess, they will be lifted up into pride. To ascend from the earth, then, is to be raised up in pride because of earthly things.

And it had two horns like a Lamb’s. The Lamb is Christ, of whom John says: “Behold the Lamb of God” (John 1). His two horns are innocence and a pure life, and doctrine and miracles. The ministers of Antichrist will pretend to possess these two horns: innocence and a pure life, doctrine and miracles. What Christ and his ministers possess in truth, these men will possess deceptively.

And it spoke like a dragon—that is, just as formerly the devil spoke through the serpent with evil persuasion to the woman, through whom he deceived the man, so these men, through their perverse teaching, lead astray as many as they can and separate them from the faith of Christ. Although they are savage dragons, pouring the poison of wickedness into their hearers, they pretend to be lambs so that they may be able to deceive lambs. They assume the Lamb’s appearance so that they may carry out the dragon’s work.

And it exercised all the authority of the first beast in its presence. Just as Antichrist deceives through force and fraud, flattery and teachings, terrors and torments, so do all his ministers.

But what does “in its presence” mean? Will the preachers of Antichrist always be able to remain in his presence? No. Rather, they will travel through every region of the world preaching. But wherever they may be, they will strive to do what they know pleases him, as though they were always seen by him and stood in his presence. They will honor him so greatly that whatever they are about to do, they will say they are doing before him, as though nothing could be hidden from him.

For just as the saints, because they continually keep his will, confess that they remain in God’s presence—according to the words: “The Lord lives, before whom I stand” (1 Kings 17)—and as the Apostle says: “As from God, in the presence of God, we speak in Christ” (2 Cor. 12), so they will place their head before them in everything they say and do, as though they exercised authority over the people in his presence [Col. 1099B].

And it made the earth—that is, the earthly bodies of human beings—and those who dwell on the earth—that is, souls resting in bodies and placing all their concern in earthly things—worship the first beast, that is, Antichrist, of whom he had said above: “I saw a beast ascending from the sea, having seven heads,” and so forth.

Whose mortal wound was healed—that is, the one who pretends to have risen from the dead, as was already said above. All who receive him will worship him, prostrated in both body and soul; and in that condemned man they will worship the devil dwelling in him. Here the exceedingly grave power of the deceptions is shown, by which both souls and bodies are miserably enslaved. For one who falls by force, without being deceived, is captivated in body alone. But one who is deceived is captivated both in mind and body.

And it performed great signs, because it will deceive many not only by words but also by false miracles, so that it might even make fire descend from heaven in the sight of human beings. Concerning this the Lord says in the Gospel: “False Christs and false prophets will arise, and they will give signs and wonders, so as to lead astray, if possible, even the elect” (Matt. 24). Among these signs and miracles, the greatest will be that it will make fire descend from heaven.

We read in the Old Testament that, by the just judgment and permission of God, the devil caused fire to descend from heaven upon the flocks of blessed Job; it consumed the sheep and the servants. What wonder, then, if through Antichrist he is going to do what he has already done through himself? [Col. 1099D] Yet he will not do this by his own power but by God’s permission, so that those who believe him may be deceived by God’s just judgment.

Alternatively: we read in the Acts of the Apostles that on Pentecost the Holy Spirit descended upon the apostles in the appearance of fire. Filled with it, they began to speak in various languages of the mighty works of God (Acts 3). They also subsequently gave the Holy Spirit to those whom they baptized, so that they too might speak in all languages, as we read that Peter and the others did.

Hence Simon, bringing money, said: “Give me this power, so that whoever receives the laying on of my hands may receive the Holy Spirit, so that he may be able to speak in all languages.” Thus they made fire descend from heaven—that is, from themselves—namely, the Holy Spirit, of whom the Lord says: “I have come to cast fire upon the earth” (Matt. 7), that is, upon those who had previously been earthly but would then be renewed by the grace of the Holy Spirit.

Therefore the Lord himself specifically said that this would occur as a sign of believers: “These signs will accompany those who believe: In my name they will cast out demons; they will speak in new languages” (Mark 16). Thus this beast will make fire descend from heaven, because the preachers of Antichrist will falsely imitate this by pretending, through the laying on of hands, to give the Holy Spirit to their followers.

For this reason the persecution will be more intense, since it will be thought that the beast either possesses or can give that gift of the Holy Spirit by which the Lord willed his Church to excel above all the kingdoms of the world. Although heretics appear to share many things with us, the Church alone boasts that she possesses this particular gift [Col. 1100B].

Perhaps they will use certain tricks so that those upon whom they lay hands will speak in the languages of many peoples. And this will be done in the sight of people who understand according to the flesh. Those who savor not divine things but human things are called “human beings,” because by this deception they are shown to be mocking not the eyes of spiritual people but of carnal ones.

Alternatively: we read in the Old Testament that, at Elijah’s word, fire descended from heaven and consumed two companies of fifty, together with their fifty men. Elijah’s word, therefore, was fire; and they themselves summoned fire against themselves mockingly, crying: “Man of God, come down; the king summons you.”

Fire, then, is understood as the fervor and zeal by which the saints—Elijah, Enoch, and the other preachers—are inflamed against those whom they see departing from the faith. Kindled by the zeal of their fervor, they will condemn them with their anathema. Thus the beast will make fire descend from heaven, because the reprobate, acting perversely, will kindle themselves with the flames of zeal against the heavenly souls of the elect, so that they may condemn them.

This is also what was said above: “If anyone wishes to harm them, fire will go out from their mouth and devour their enemies.”

And it will deceive those who dwell on the earth because of the signs that were given it to perform in the presence of the beast, telling those who dwell on the earth to make an image of the beast that had the wound of the sword and lived. By “earth,” as has often been said, earthly people are understood—those who can therefore be deceived by the ministers of Antichrist because they love earthly things more than heavenly ones.

They will make an image of the beast [Col. 1100D]—that is, they will hold his faith and imitate his deception. We must not understand this childishly, as though they were going to make some image that they would carry about with them. Rather, they will make his image—that is, they will possess his faith and imitate his deception—as though he were truly the Son of God and had truly risen from the dead.

He has the wound of the sword and lived, according to what was said above, because Antichrist will say that he was killed and rose from the dead. In the presence of this beast they will perform many signs by which they will deceive the earth. Wherever they may be, they will fulfill his will and do what they know pleases him, as though they were always standing before him.

And it was given to it to give breath to the image of the beast [Col. 1101A]. That is, it was given to the ministers of Antichrist by God—that is, it was permitted to them—to give breath to the image of the beast. The image of the beast is understood as the condemned man himself, in whom the devil will dwell. The false preachers will give him breath—that is, they will say that the fullness of the Holy Spirit rests in him.

For we say: “Give honor to God.” And again: “I will exalt you, my God and king” (Ps. 29). How can we give him honor, or how can we exalt him, when he has nothing by which he may be exalted? We exalt him when we proclaim him exalted. In this way they will give breath to the image of the beast, proclaiming that he is full of divinity.

For Photinus also says: “I grant Christ a beginning from Mary”—that is, “I announce that he took his beginning from Mary.”

And that the image of the beast might speak [Col. 1101B]—“it was given to it” is understood. For they will not only say that the Holy Spirit rests in him; they will also preach that he speaks—that is, that through the spirit of prophecy he foretells the future. He will prevail to such an extent through signs and miracles that he will be believed by his followers to be full of the Holy Spirit and will be thought capable of predicting what is to come. For the devil will speak through his mouth and will give his worshipers many deceptive responses, just as formerly he spoke through the mouths of idols.

And it will cause all who do not worship the image of the beast to be killed. That is, whoever does not obey them by worshiping Antichrist as God will be killed by them and by the rulers of this age who follow them, as will happen to Elijah, Enoch, and many others.

And it will cause all—the small and the great, the rich and the poor, the free and the slaves—to receive a mark on their right hand or on their foreheads.

The small are those who cannot accomplish the evil that they understand and desire. The great are those who practice evil according to their own inclination. The rich are those who possess earthly goods, or who are also proud. In contrast, “blessed are the poor in spirit.” He will also enrich his ministers with many riches, by which they will be lifted up into excessive pride.

The poor are understood as those poor in faith and good works. In contrast, the Apostle says of himself and those like him: “As having nothing and possessing everything” (2 Cor. 6)—that is, “you were strangers to righteousness.” The free and the slaves are those alienated from righteousness and made slaves of sins. To such people the Apostle says: “When you were slaves of sin, you were free from righteousness” (Rom. 6)—that is, “you were strangers to righteousness.”

These people have the mark of the beast on their right hands and on their foreheads, and even now they exist both outside and within the Church. Outside the Church are the Jews; within it are false Christians.

What is understood by the right hand of the reprobate except their activity? And what is expressed by the forehead except faith? Thus they have the mark on their right hand and forehead, because where they ought to have pure works of virtue and faith, they are found disfigured by the stain of crime.

The Jews have his mark on their hand because they perform the works of the devil; on their forehead because they believe in him and await his coming, according to the words: “I have come in my Father’s name, and you did not receive me; another will come in his own name, and him you will receive.”

Likewise, those who verbally possess the faith but do not possess the works of faith also have it. Properly, however, this refers to that time when the wicked will openly follow him with reprobate faith and reprobate action.

And so that no one may be able to buy or sell except one who has the mark, or the name of the beast, or the number of its name. This commerce is to be understood spiritually. For the Lord, entrusting his faithful with such great talents of teaching, says: “Trade until I come.” And preaching is rightly compared with commerce. Holy teachers pay out teaching and receive faith from the peoples; they impart faith and immediately receive their way of life.

At the time of Antichrist, therefore, none of these people—that is, none of the good preachers—will be able to buy or sell. That is, no one will be able to preach Christ freely [Col. 1102B], because they will be shut up in prisons and, moreover, killed, except one who has the mark of the beast—that is, who has held his faith, his name, and the number of his name, about which we shall speak below.

The mark and the name of the beast, and the number of its name, are one and the same. Yet this commerce will not cease among those who have been chosen, because, as far as they are able, they will strive to distribute the talent of the divine word.

For to this marketplace those outstanding merchants will come: namely, Elijah and Enoch. In view of the wares, they will display the glorious goods of the Church, so that not only those devoted to the Christian faith but even those who appeared to bear the mark of the beast may desire them. Of one of them the Lord says: “When Elijah comes, he will restore all things to you.”

Here is wisdom: Let the one who has understanding—that is, the ability to penetrate these matters by understanding them—calculate the number of the beast. Blessed John, considering the obscurity of this passage, wished to make the reader attentive; for this reason he warned him in advance to discern the number of the beast. And because Antichrist will be a mere human being, though filled with a demon, he adds: For it is the number of a human being.

It is as though he said: “Pay close attention, because he will be a true human being, not God, as he himself will boast.” And its number is six hundred and sixty-six.

All the books of the New Testament were written in the Greek language, except the Gospel of Matthew and Paul’s Epistle to the Hebrews. Since this book too, like the others, was written in Greek, the meaning of this passage must therefore be sought according to Greek usage, among whom all letters contain numerical values.

Let us therefore propose ANTEMOS, which is interpreted as “opposed to honor.” This name suits him well, since he is called Antichrist—that is, opposed to Christ. For this name contains within it the following number:

- α signifies one;
- ν, fifty;
- τ, three hundred;
- ε, five;
- μ, forty;
- ο, seventy;
- σ, two hundred.

Let us propose another form as well: ARNUME, which is interpreted as “I deny.” This name also suits him, because he will deny that Christ is God and will unjustly confess himself to be God. In this name too the number itself is contained:

- α signifies one;
- ρ, one hundred;
- ν, fifty;
- ο, seventy;
- ν, four hundred;
- μ, forty;
- ε, five.

Added together, these make six hundred and sixty-six.

Let us propose yet another: TEITAN, which in Latin is called *sol*, “sun.” The sun, by signification, is Christ, who enlightens every human being coming into this world (John 1). Teitan is also called a giant; hence we read in Virgil: “the Titan stars.” Christ is the giant of whom the Psalmist says: “He rejoiced like a giant” (Ps. 18).

Antichrist himself will therefore falsely appropriate this name and say that he is that sun of which it is written: “For you who fear my name, the sun of righteousness will rise.” The letters of this name likewise contain the entire preceding number, namely six hundred and sixty-six:

- τ signifies three hundred;
- ε, five;
- ι, ten;
- τ again, three hundred;
- α, one;
- ν, fifty.

Added together, these make six hundred and sixty-six.

As we have said, Antichrist will appropriate this name for himself, daring to proclaim himself to human beings as the light, although he is an apostate angel transforming himself into an angel of light.

For this reason, if anyone also wishes to understand this in another way, let us set down the name in Latin letters in which the same number is found, as follows: Dic Lux, “Say: Light.” For he will confess himself to be the light, as was said. The letters signify:

- d, five hundred;
- i, one;
- c, one hundred;
- l, fifty;
- v, five;
- x, ten.

Collected together, these likewise make six hundred and sixty-six.

We can also find the same number if it is written in Greek letters, in a Gothic name, as follows: GENSERIKOS. For:

- γ signifies three;
- ε, five;
- ν, fifty;
- σ, two hundred;
- η, eight;
- ρ, one hundred;
- ι, ten;
- κ, twenty;
- ο, seventy;
- σ, two hundred.

Added together, these make six hundred and sixty-six.

The interpretation of the name is “deceiver of the nations”: in this respect he is opposed to Christ, since the one is called a deceiver, whereas the other is called the Savior of the nations.

Whether, therefore, this number is understood in this way or that, whether in Greek, Latin, or Gothic, it is not unfittingly referred to the person of Antichrist.

But there is still something about this same number that we must weigh through subtle investigation, so that, by offering the reader more concerning it, we may satisfy him more fully. Let it therefore be said: “For his number is the six-hundred-and-sixty-sixth.”

The number six is considered perfect in secular learning because it is the first number completed by its own parts: by its sixth, third, and half—namely, one, two, and three—which, added together, make six. No other number before six is found whose whole sum is completed when it is divided by its parts; and when it rises from its sixth part—that is, from one—to ten, and from its third part to twenty, it produces, as it were, a square ten.

But to make it solid, again, from its sixth part, which rises to ten, it reaches one hundred, and thus, multiplied through its parts, completes six hundred.

Yet because, by advancing through the loftiness of sacred Scripture, we transcend all these considerations, there we find where six, sixty, and one hundred derive their perfection. In sacred Scripture the number six is perfect because, at the creation of the world, the Lord completed on the sixth day by his work what he had begun on the first day, when he made the human being—on whose account he had created all things—in his own image.

The number ten is perfect in it because the law is contained in ten commandments, and every fault is restrained by no more than ten words. Moreover, as the Truth declares, the workers in the vineyard will be rewarded with ten.

The number sixty is perfect in it because everything performed in six days is enclosed within those same commandments of the Decalogue; and, as the Gospel’s word testifies, the good earth produces a sixtieth-fold harvest.

The number one hundred is perfect in it because, by multiplying the commandments of the Decalogue ten times, it encompasses the whole sum of activity. For if the number one hundred did not signify perfection, the Lord would never have said to the disciples: “Everyone who has left house, or brothers, or sisters, or father, or mother, or children, or fields, for my name’s sake, will receive a hundredfold and will possess eternal life” (Matt. 19).

Since God completed all his works in six days, and since there are six ages of this world, we may rightly understand by this number the whole duration of the present life [Col. 1104B].

Since, therefore, that man, the son of perdition, will falsely assert that he is Christ—as though he himself were the creator of all the things that unfold through the six days—and will falsely claim to be alpha and omega, beginning and end, God before the ages and man at the end of the ages, the number of the beast, rightly calculated by understanding, namely six hundred and sixty-six, encompasses the whole duration of the present life and reveals both the wickedness of diabolical fraud and the final end of the world.

## CHAPTER XIV

And I saw, and behold, the Lamb was standing upon Mount Zion, and with him one hundred and forty-four thousand having his name—that is, Christ’s name—and the name of his Father—that is, of God the Father—written on their foreheads.

Zion, which is interpreted “watching,” is the Church, which unceasingly contemplates the good things to come and also declares what evils are to be avoided. Mount Zion is nothing other than Zion itself, that is, the Church, of which the Psalmist says: “Mother Zion shall say, ‘A man’” (Ps. 86), and elsewhere: “Those who trust in the Lord are like Mount Zion” (Ps. 124).

The Lamb is Christ, of whom John says: “Behold the Lamb of God” (John 1). The Lamb stood upon Mount Zion because Christ himself presides over his Church. But here a definite number is put for an indefinite one: one hundred and forty-four thousand for the innumerable multitude of the elect. More particularly, this number signifies those who are virgins both in mind and body, for many are virgins in body but not in mind.

For the very words by which one hundred and forty-four thousand are said to have been seen with the Lord are not without mystery. The number one hundred is often shown in divine Scripture to be perfect; hence: “The good earth produced fruit a hundredfold,” which is shown to belong to virginal perfection. Again: “A certain man had a hundred sheep.” In this passage the total number of angels and human beings is understood: God Almighty had one hundred sheep because he created the nature of angels and human beings to behold him. And again: “Whoever leaves house and brothers,” and so forth, up to: “He shall receive a hundredfold and possess eternal life.”

The number forty also is consecrated in mystery; hence the Lord himself fasted for forty days, as Moses and Elijah had formerly done. For it consists of four and ten. Four is sacred because of the four rivers of Paradise, or the four books of the Gospel, or the four well-known parts of the world, or also the four principal virtues. Ten likewise is consecrated because of the ten commandments of the law. We then fulfil the Decalogue of the law when we keep the four books of the Gospel in faith and conduct.

A thousand likewise is often used for the perfection of the matter in question; hence: “The word which he commanded for a thousand generations.” Since one must believe that the world will by no means extend even to one hundred generations, what else is signified by a thousand generations except the totality of generations? Thus also in this Apocalypse the saints are said to reign with Christ for a thousand years, that is, forever and through all future times.

Therefore, as stated, this number expresses the total of those who are virgins in mind and body. It should consequently be considered that, if the number of those who have preserved virginity, such as John and Paul, will be so great, the other saints will be far more numerous. It should also be noted here that these are said to stand upon Mount Zion when they themselves are Mount Zion, because no one will triumph over the beast unless he rises even above himself. For one who has entered into combat against the prince of this world must stand at great elevation of mind.

It should also be observed that the Lamb is here said to stand, whereas Luke says of him: “The Lord Jesus ascended into heaven and sits at the right hand of God” (Acts 1). We should therefore know that sitting belongs to one who reigns or judges, but standing to one who labors or helps. Since, after death had been overcome, authority in heaven and on earth was given to Christ risen from the dead, Luke rightly says that he sits. Thus Stephen too, surrounded by those casting stones, looking into heaven, said: “Behold, I see the heavens opened and Jesus standing at the right hand of the power of God” (Acts 7).

The elect also stand with him because they labor in the present life and are placed in combat. Having his name and the name of his Father written on their foreheads. We should not understand this carnally, as though they had little labels bound around their foreheads on which the name of the Lamb or of his Father was written. Rather, they bear on their foreheads the name of the Lamb and of the Father, whose faith they hold and adorn with works; and because they are marked in the name of the Father and the Son, they are protected from every adversity by this sign of the cross.

And I heard a voice from heaven like the voice of many waters, and like the voice of great thunder. And the voice that I heard was like that of harpists playing their harps. Heaven is the Church itself; for this reason those who sit with the Lamb are themselves heaven. And because, by the Lord’s mercy, many virgins are to be gathered from all nations, their voice is said to be like the voice of many waters. For, as John himself says, many waters are many peoples.

And because such persons also belong to the number of judges and are preachers—as John himself was, and Paul, who says: “I desire all to be as myself” (1 Cor. 7)—it is therefore said: “And like the voice of great thunder.” They too are harpists, imitating the passion of their Lord. For, as was said above, in a harp there is wood and strings stretched in different ways. This wood is the wood of the Lord’s passion, or of the cross. The strings, moreover, are the devoted hearts of the saints, who, imitating and recalling his passion, mortify themselves with their vices and desires, fulfilling in their body what is lacking in the sufferings of Christ.

And they were singing, as it were, a new song before the throne and before the four living creatures and the elders. To sing a new song is to rejoice in the incorrupt integrity of mind and body. [Col. 1106B] But since they themselves are the throne, the four living creatures, and the elders, what does it mean that they are said to sing before the throne, the four living creatures, and the elders? Clearly, they always stand before themselves, since no change among mutable things turns their minds away from contemplation of the Creator. And no one could sing the song—that is, no one could rejoice in the incorrupt virginity of mind and body—except those hundred and forty-four thousand: not Peter, certainly, nor any other apostle who had experienced marriage. For even in marriage the Psalmist recognizes sin, saying: “For behold, I was conceived in iniquities, and in sins my mother brought me forth” (Psalm 50).

[Col. 1106C] Nevertheless, we may say what we do not dare confidently to affirm as true: that not all virgins precede the married in that blessed kingdom, but specifically those who, in life, conduct, and the suffering of martyrdom, while also preserving virginity, are made equal to married martyrs.
